title: Palermo: Improving the Performance of Oblivious Memory using Protocol-Hardware Co-Design
problem: Oblivious RAM (ORAM) protocols impose severe performance penalties because classical ORAM enforces strict sequential dependencies between memory operations, leaving memory bandwidth severely underutilized. Prior prefetching and request-elimination approaches are fragile under low-locality workloads and create additional ORAM stash pressure overhead.
motivation: ORAM is essential for data-privacy guarantees in secure enclaves and trusted hardware, but its high overhead makes it impractical for real workloads without hardware acceleration that exploits parallelism.
method: Palermo redesigns the RingORAM protocol to allow overlapping of memory operations both within a single ORAM request and across multiple concurrent requests, without violating correctness or security invariants. A dedicated ORAM controller hardware implements this relaxed protocol by concurrently issuing memory requests while tracking and enforcing only the necessary inter-request dependencies to maintain a consistent ORAM tree view. The architecture manages stash and position-map structures in hardware to prevent stash overflow while enabling pipelined DRAM accesses.
key_novelty: A protocol-hardware co-design that removes artificial sequential constraints in classical ORAM, enabling concurrent multi-request memory access without breaking security or correctness guarantees.
contributions: New ORAM protocol that legally overlaps memory operations within and across ORAM requests
Hardware ORAM controller that enforces only necessary dependencies, maximizing memory bandwidth utilization
2.9x average speedup over RingORAM with negligible area overhead (<2% of 12th-gen Intel CPU after scaling)
Demonstrated superiority over state-of-the-art PageORAM, PrORAM, and IR-ORAM

metrics.area: 5.78mm^2 ORAM controller (<2% overhead in 12th-gen Intel CPU after technology scaling)

limitations: Evaluation focuses on simulated workloads; real end-to-end secure enclave integration and overhead analysis not provided.
primary_theme: ORAM protocol-hardware co-design for bandwidth-efficient secure memory
